findings.title: Settings POST whitelist omits shutdown_drain_timeout — any configured value silently resets to 60.0 on next settings save
findings.problem: The new GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout field is added in this diff, but the settings POST handler (save_settings) builds new_config["general"] as an EXPLICIT field whitelist (routes.py:539-550) rather than merging over current_settings.general. Any key not in that literal is absent from the dict passed to SettingsModel(**new_config), so Pydantic fills it with the field default (60.0). _settings_to_dict then does settings.general.model_dump() and _atomic_toml_write does a full-file os.replace — so the reverted 60.0 is written to triggarr.toml, overwriting whatever the operator had set. Concretely: an operator hand-edits shutdown_drain_timeout = 300.0 into triggarr.toml, restarts, then later toggles skip_unreleased in the UI — their 300.0 is silently reset to 60.0 with no warning. This is a pre-existing structural hazard of the whitelist pattern that this diff newly exposes; note the whitelist already handles exactly this case for tracking_delay_seconds, which has no form input and is explicitly carried forward via `current_settings.general.tracking_delay_seconds`. Phase plan 75-02 is scheduled to add the form input and the safe_float POST parse line, which would close this. The window is real but bounded: it exists only between plan 75-01 (this diff) and 75-02 landing. Flagging because 75-01 is committed as its own atomic commit and the field is documented in the diff comment as operator-settable ('Config value is the default'), so a partial-phase ship or an abandoned 75-02 leaves a data-loss-on-save knob live.
findings.fix_hint: Plan 75-02 adds `"shutdown_drain_timeout": safe_float(form.get("shutdown_drain_timeout"), 60.0, 1.0, 3600.0)`. Until it lands, carry the field forward like tracking_delay_seconds does: `"shutdown_drain_timeout": current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout`.
findings.why_it_matters: Silent reversion of a persisted operator setting on an unrelated save is a data-loss class bug — the operator gets no error, and the shorter drain (60s vs their 300s) only manifests as truncated in-flight search cycles at the next shutdown, far from the action that caused it.

findings.title: Wire the configured timeout into the shutdown drain
findings.problem: Setting general.shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 is accepted, but shutdown still uses _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT in scheduler.py:634. That constant is initialized at import from the environment or a hardcoded 60.0; no runtime code reads the new field. With no environment override, a cycle needing more than 60 seconds still hits forced resource closure despite the configured longer drain.
